position.description:
ADOLESCENT SERVICES MANAGER

On-Site | Davie, FL | Monday-Friday | Full-Time 

About the Role

Lead the day-to-day experience of an adolescent mental health program where structure, consistency, and connection matter. You’ll lead the team and systems that keep each day running smoothly while creating a safe, supportive environment for adolescents and families. This role is ideal for someone who can lead people, create structure, solve problems, and build an environment where adolescents can succeed.

Backgrounds that translate well: Education · School Administration · Student Services · Youth Programs · Behavioral Health · Program Management

What You'll Do

• Lead the daily adolescent program experience, maintaining a safe, structured, and welcoming environment
• Supervise Wellness Coordinators through clear expectations, coaching, feedback, and accountability
• Keep daily program flow on track, including staff coverage, schedules, attendance, census, and intake coordination
• Build positive relationships with adolescents and help the team respond effectively to behavioral, emotional, and day-to-day needs
• Partner with therapists, families, and program leadership to support a consistent client experience
• Monitor documentation, incident reporting, safety protocols, and compliance requirements
• Anticipate challenges, respond calmly in the moment, and keep the program on track through changes
• Coordinate facility, supply, and administrative needs that impact the adolescent experience

What We're Looking For

• 2+ years of experience in education, school administration, youth services, behavioral health, program management, or team leadership
• Experience supervising or leading others
• Strong organization and ability to manage multiple priorities and changing needs
• Confident setting expectations, providing feedback, and holding others accountable
• Calm, solutions-focused approach to challenging situations
• Strong attention to documentation, policies, safety, and established processes
• Ability to connect with adolescents while maintaining appropriate structure and boundaries
• Eligible for DCF and AHCA Level 2 background screening and drug testing
• Bachelor's degree preferred; equivalent experience considered

About AWA

AWA provides adolescent mental health PHP and IOP services across South Florida. We support teens and families through structured, compassionate environments designed to help adolescents grow.

Learn More: Adolescent Wellness Academy

candidates.cover_letter:
To Whom it May Concern:

I am excited to apply for the Adolescent Services Manager position with AWA. With more than 15 years of experience working with adolescents, leading interdisciplinary teams, coordinating programs, and partnering with families, I believe my background in education translates directly to the structure, leadership, and relationship-building required in this role.

Throughout my career as a middle school educator, I have been responsible for creating safe, structured environments where adolescents with different needs, personalities, and challenges could succeed. I regularly worked with students experiencing academic, behavioral, and interpersonal difficulties and collaborated with families, counselors, administrators, and colleagues to address concerns and develop effective solutions. My experience has taught me how important consistency, clear expectations, appropriate boundaries, and strong relationships are when working with adolescents.

In my role as an Academic Team Leader, I led an interdisciplinary team of educators across multiple subject areas, facilitated meetings, coordinated responsibilities, mentored colleagues, and served as a liaison between staff and administration. I also served as a primary point of contact for parents, including during sensitive situations requiring thoughtful communication and problem-solving. These experiences have prepared me to provide clear expectations, support staff, and help maintain consistent program operations.

My experience also extends beyond the classroom. As a coach of three middle school athletic programs, I provided structure, mentorship, accountability, and behavioral guidance while communicating directly with families. As the coordinator of a large Washington, D.C. student trip, I managed schedules, logistics, multiple stakeholders, changing circumstances, and unexpected problems while maintaining a safe and organized experience for students.

I was also nominated for the 2024–25 District Teacher of the Year Award, recognition that reflects the relationships I built with students, families, and colleagues and the leadership I brought to my school community.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to apply the leadership and adolescent-support skills I have developed throughout my career in a mental health setting. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA's work with adolescents and families while continuing to grow as a program leader.

Thank you for your consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to your adolescent services team.

Sincerely,
Timothy Baker

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am very interested in the Adolescent Services Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. After more than 30 years in Human Resources, employee benefits, wellness, risk management, and organizational leadership, I am at a point in my career where I am intentionally looking to bring my experience into work that is more directly focused on people, wellbeing, and positive outcomes.

Throughout my career, I have worked with employees and families navigating difficult situations, coordinated wellness and health-related programs, managed sensitive matters requiring discretion and good judgment, and partnered with professionals across many disciplines. I have also spent many years coaching, educating, presenting, and helping people understand their options during stressful or unfamiliar circumstances.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the combination of structure, relationship building, team coordination, and creating a supportive environment for young people. My background has taught me how important consistency, communication, accountability, empathy, and appropriate boundaries are when working with people who may be facing challenges.

In addition to my professional HR background, health and wellness have always been important to me personally and professionally. Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Adolescent Program Lead position. My background is in higher education, student support, community engagement, and program coordination, and I am interested in this role because it combines working directly with young people with the responsibility of keeping a program organized, consistent, and supportive.

In my current role at Nova Southeastern University, I work directly with prospective students and families, helping them understand university programs, services, and resources while serving as a point of contact throughout the recruitment process. I also coordinate student recruitment programs, supervise and train student employees and volunteers, maintain attendance and program records, and work with different departments to make sure programs run effectively. This has taught me how important structure and communication are when working with students and families, particularly when there are multiple needs to manage at the same time.

Previously, as a Community Engagement Specialist with Durham/Duke Community Affairs, I worked directly with community members and students to provide information, identify needs, and connect people with appropriate resources and services. I also planned community programs and events, coordinated volunteers, maintained program documentation, and worked with community partners to improve programming based on participant needs. I also have earlier experience working with youth through summer programming, as well as experience providing direct services and resource referrals through the Criminal Justice Resource Center. Across these positions, I have learned that helping people is not only about being approachable. While my professional background is not specifically in behavioral health, I believe my experience in student services, youth programming, community support, and program coordination translates well to this position. I would bring a practical, calm, and people-focused approach to supporting the adolescents, families, and staff involved in the program.

Thank you for your consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to your program.

Sincerely,

Dear Hiring Manager:

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Operations Supervisor – Adolescent Mental Health position with AWA. With more than 20 years of supervisory and operational experience, along with a Master of Science in Forensic Psychology, I offer a strong combination of people leadership, organizational oversight, crisis response, documentation, and compliance awareness.

In my current role as a Public Safety Supervisor at the Miami Beach Convention Center, I help manage daily operations in a fast-paced environment where safety, coverage, communication, and accountability are essential. My responsibilities include coordinating staff assignments, addressing callouts and coverage needs, providing clear direction, monitoring performance, responding to incidents, preparing detailed reports, and communicating operational concerns to leadership and outside agencies. Throughout my career, I have remained calm under pressure, managed competing priorities, de-escalated difficult situations, and ensured that established procedures were followed.

Although my professional background has primarily been in public safety and operations, my graduate education in forensic psychology provides a valuable foundation for working within an adolescent mental health setting. My studies strengthened my understanding of human behavior, crisis intervention, community-based challenges, trauma, and the importance of treating individuals and families with patience, dignity, and respect. I understand that this position is not a clinical role, but one that ensures the program remains organized, appropriately staffed, compliant, and responsive to the needs of clients, families, and clinical personnel.

I would bring to AWA a structured yet compassionate leadership style, strong documentation and incident-management skills, and the ability to communicate clearly with employees, clinicians, families, and leadership. I am confident delegating responsibilities, following up on assignments, addressing performance concerns, and identifying operational risks before they interfere with service delivery.

AWA’s commitment to supporting adolescents and their families strongly resonates with me. I would welcome the opportunity to apply my leadership experience and educational background to help maintain a safe, organized, and client-centered program.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications can contribute to AWA’s mission.

Sincerely,

LeAnn Cintron

candidates.cover_letter:
To Adolescent Wellness Academy,

	My name is Daniela Gutierrez, I am an active immigration paralegal in the Children’s Legal Program with background and experience as a Case Manager with the Office of Refugee Resettlement. I write to express my interest in the Adolescence Service Manager position. My academic background in Psychology and experience as a Case Manager for unaccompanied children with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) has equipped me with the skill and tact necessary to manage crisis intervention and trauma-informed care for resident youth. As an experienced paralegal, I hold skills and experience in various matters I believe to be beneficial to you and your clients. 

When working with youth, communication is my top-priority to ensure clients feel safe, informed and comfortable with their Legal and care team as they navigate the tough and complex legal system. In immigration, it is not uncommon to have a case where abuse is involved, and it is extremely important to be able to identify when a client may be in an unsafe environment and know how to approach these situations with sensitivity, delicacy and care. As a case manager, I was responsible for approximately 8 in-house residents at a time, who recently immigrated from their home country and served as their intermediate stay between ICE custody release and family reunification. During their placement, I worked closely with their counseling team and teachers to provide curated service plans and goals while in the program, for the duration of their family reunification case. Through this experience, I have learned how to balance casework with strict deadlines, adhering to program policies and procedures, and maintaining an organized system and effective task management, while simultaneously providing empathetic and sensitive support to our resident boys ages 13-17, going through a difficult reunification process or legal conflicts, experienced recent traumatic events or dealing with a troubled past, and current ongoing therapeutic sessions which may impact behavior. 

As a legal assistant, my responsibility is to serve as a point-of-contact to ensure clients are attended to throughout their case’s progression and to relay important information in a timely manner. It is of high-priority to me, being fluent in Spanish, that Spanish-speaking clients are not excluded in familiarity, understanding and clarity of their entire legal progress. It is crucial to provide clients legal services with empathy and reassurance they have someone to depend on as they are dealing with the emotions behind legal matters. Throughout my professional career, I have recognized the importance of maintaining detailed records as well as documentation and reporting of significant events relevant to a client’s casework.  

After navigating the hurdles of immigration law, I’m dedicated to bring my knowledge and skills in a new field while utilizing my expertise in family matters and delicate events or trauma. My capabilities of excelling in this position are not limited to the skills I've considered in this letter. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss what my experience and background can offer you and your clients to establish strong rapport and deliver effective care.

Sincerely,

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,
Some of the most meaningful work we can do is help a young person recognize that their current circumstances do not have to define their future. That is what draws me to the Adolescent Service Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy.
My career has given me the opportunity to work with individuals across a wide range of ages and needs, but two experiences in particular have shaped the way I approach behavioral health and service leadership: my work with adolescents at Dade Juvenile Detention Center and my most recent role as Assistant Administrator at Midtown Assisted Living Residence, a community serving adults ages 18–75 with Limited Mental Health diagnoses.
At Dade Juvenile Detention Center, I worked directly with adolescents experiencing mental health challenges and substance-use issues. That experience taught me something that has stayed with me throughout my career: behavior is often communication. Behind anger, defiance, withdrawal, or poor decisions can be a young person who is struggling, afraid, overwhelmed, or simply does not yet have the tools to express what they need. Working with adolescents requires structure and accountability, but it also requires patience, consistency, emotional intelligence, and the ability to build trust.
My experience at Midtown allowed me to take those skills into a leadership role. As Assistant Administrator, I was responsible for supporting the day-to-day operations of a behavioral health environment while working closely with residents, families, staff, healthcare professionals, and outside partners. I managed challenging situations, supported crisis intervention and de-escalation efforts, addressed staff performance and training needs, and helped maintain compliance within a highly regulated environment.
I also bring a strong people-operations and leadership background. As a SHRM-CP certified professional, I understand that successful programs depend not only on the individuals receiving services, but also on the people providing them. I believe in hiring the right people, setting clear expectations, developing staff, holding teams accountable, and creating a culture where employees understand that their work can fundamentally impact someone's life.
What I would bring to Adolescent Wellness Academy is the ability to see both sides of the operation: the human side and the leadership side. I can connect with a young person who is struggling while also understanding the importance of documentation, policies, staffing, compliance, communication, and operational accountability.
Most importantly, I don't believe adolescents should be defined by their diagnosis, their mistakes, their circumstances, or the hardest chapter of their lives. I believe our responsibility as professionals is to help create an environment where they can develop the skills, confidence, and support necessary to write a different chapter.
I would be honored to bring my experience, leadership, and passion for behavioral health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am excited about the possibility of contributing to a team that is doing work that can have a lasting impact on the lives of young people and their families.
Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss what I can bring to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team.
Sincerely,
Tia Baskin

Sincerely,

I am excited to apply for an opportunity with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor’s degree in Kinesiology/Exercise Science from Elizabeth City State University and a professional background in youth development, leadership, program coordination, operations, and customer service, I am eager to bring my experience to an organization dedicated to supporting adolescents and their families.

My passion for working with young people began through my experience in higher education, where I served in multiple residential leadership roles, including Resident Hall Director and Area Coordinator. In these positions, I supervised and developed Resident Advisors, provided guidance and support to students, organized community and personal-development programs, managed daily operations, resolved conflicts, and responded to emergency and crisis situations. These experiences taught me the importance of creating an environment where young people feel supported, respected, safe, and heard. They also strengthened my ability to remain calm under pressure, communicate effectively with individuals from different backgrounds, recognize when additional support is needed, and work collaboratively with a larger team.

My Exercise Science education further strengthened my interest in health, wellness, human development, anatomy, physiology, and helping individuals improve their overall well-being. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to bring that educational foundation into a setting where I can continue developing professionally while making a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents.

In my current role with Enterprise Mobility, I have continued developing strong skills in communication, problem-solving, customer service, documentation, compliance, and fast-paced operations. My combined background has allowed me to become a dependable leader who can manage competing priorities, build relationships, coach others, and take ownership of challenging situations.

I believe my combination of Exercise Science education, youth-development experience, leadership background, and operational skills would allow me to make a positive contribution to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to continue learning about adolescent behavioral health and to grow within an organization whose mission aligns with my passion for helping others.

Upon selection, I would bring a leadership style grounded in organization, accountability, communication, safety, and collaboration. My goal would be to help ensure that the program operates efficiently while never losing sight of the community it serves.

Dear Hiring Manager,

My professional background combines education, youth development, program management, staff supervision, safety, and student support, along with academic training in Homeland Security, Criminal Justice, and Psychology. I am passionate about creating structured, supportive environments where young people can feel safe, respected, encouraged, and equipped to succeed.

My educational background further supports my interest in this position. While my professional experience has been primarily in education and youth programs rather than clinical mental-health care, I believe my combination of leadership, operations, youth support, safety, communication, and psychology-related education provides a strong foundation for contributing to an adolescent mental-health program.

I would be honored to bring my leadership experience, organizational skills, compassion, and commitment to youth development to your organization. I am confident in my ability to support program operations, build strong working relationships, supervise teams, communicate effectively with families and professionals, and help maintain a safe and positive environment for adolescents.

Dear Hiring Manager:

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Program Operations Supervisor – Adolescent Mental Health position. As a Florida Licensed Clinical Social Worker with more than 30 years of experience in mental health, crisis intervention, school-based behavioral health, family services, and clinical program coordination, I offer a combination of clinical expertise, leadership experience, and a strong commitment to improving outcomes for adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with children and adolescents experiencing significant emotional, behavioral, and mental-health challenges. During my tenure with Broward County Public Schools, I provided intensive individual and group therapy to students with emotional and behavioral disabilities, developed therapeutic and educational plans, collaborated with multidisciplinary teams, supported families, and provided therapeutic training to school personnel. I also served as a Head Start Social Worker and Family Counselor, providing behavioral interventions, family support, case coordination, and consultation to address barriers to students' academic, social, and emotional development.

My experience with Henderson Behavioral Health further strengthened my ability to manage complex behavioral-health situations. As a Mobile Response Team Clinician and Crisis Stabilization Unit Screener, I conducted clinical assessments, provided crisis intervention, determined appropriate levels of care, coordinated inpatient admissions, and collaborated with law enforcement, courts, healthcare providers, and community agencies. These experiences have given me a strong understanding of the operational demands involved in delivering timely, effective, and coordinated behavioral-health services.

In addition to my clinical background, I bring extensive experience working within multidisciplinary environments and coordinating services among clinicians, educators, families, administrators, and community partners. I understand the importance of maintaining high clinical standards while also ensuring that programs operate efficiently, staff receive appropriate support, documentation and regulatory requirements are met, and clients receive services that are responsive to their individual needs.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because adolescent mental health requires both strong clinical leadership and an understanding of the systems surrounding young people. Adolescents often face complex challenges involving family dynamics, school performance, trauma, behavioral concerns, substance use, peer relationships, and emerging mental-health conditions. I am passionate about helping organizations develop programs that address these needs while empowering staff to provide compassionate, evidence-informed, and culturally responsive care.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my extensive clinical experience, leadership abilities, crisis-intervention expertise, and commitment to adolescent mental health to your organization. I am confident that my background would allow me to make a meaningful contribution as a Program Operations Supervisor.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of your program.

Sincerely,

Mareo Hood, LCSW
Licensed Clinical Social Worker

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in the Learning Specialist position with your psychological and learning center. As an experienced educator with a strong background in working directly with students, developing individualized instruction, and creating supportive learning environments, I am excited about the opportunity to help children and adolescents strengthen their academic skills, executive functioning, confidence, and independence.
Throughout my teaching experience, I have worked with students with a wide range of learning styles, abilities, and educational needs. I understand that students do not all process information or develop skills in the same way, and I have learned to adjust my approach accordingly. Whether working individually with a student or in a classroom setting, I strive to provide clear structure, achievable goals, encouragement, and strategies that help students experience meaningful progress.
My background as a music educator has also given me extensive experience developing many of the executive functioning skills highlighted in this position. Learning and performing music requires sustained attention, organization, working memory, planning, self-monitoring, discipline, and the ability to break complex tasks into manageable steps. In my work with students, I regularly reinforce these skills while helping them develop effective practice and learning strategies that can transfer to other areas of their education.
I am particularly drawn to your practice’s holistic, child-centered philosophy and emphasis on collaboration among students, families, schools, and professionals. I value building positive relationships with students while maintaining structured, goal-oriented expectations. I also understand the importance of communicating clearly and professionally with parents, teachers, and colleagues to ensure that students receive consistent support.
In addition to my educational experience, I bring patience, reliability, strong interpersonal skills, and a genuine commitment to helping young people succeed. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute these strengths to your multidisciplinary team while continuing to develop my knowledge of educational therapy, executive functioning interventions, and evidence-based learning strategies.
Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could contribute to your team and the students and families you serve. I look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely,
Daniel Echazabal

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Program Operations position with AWA. As a public health professional with six years of experience in program coordination, team leadership, case management, healthcare operations, and community-based services, I have developed the organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills needed to keep complex programs running effectively while maintaining a strong focus on safety, accountability, and client experience.

In my most recent role as Program Senior Coordinator at the Association of Immunization Managers, I managed multiple public health initiatives, tracked grant requirements and deliverables, documented outcomes, coordinated stakeholders, and provided operational support to ensure programs remain on schedule. I routinely identified workflow challenges, troubleshot issues, communicated priorities, and helped teams stay organized and accountable. This experience strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining accurate documentation and attention to detail.

Previously, as a Program Coordinator, I coordinated program activities, meetings, educational webinars, and leadership development initiatives. I prepared materials, tracked milestones and action items, maintained documentation, and followed up with stakeholders to ensure outstanding tasks were completed. My experience coordinating multiple activities simultaneously has prepared me to support daily program flow, scheduling, documentation, and communication in a fast-paced environment.

I also bring direct supervisory experience from my time as a Contact Tracing Lead with the Florida Department of Health, where I managed more than 30 contact tracers during a high-volume public health response. I provided daily direction, supported staff workflows, reviewed case records for quality and completeness, addressed performance and documentation issues, and helped resolve conflicts. This experience taught me the importance of clear delegation, timely follow-up, accountability, and remaining calm when priorities change quickly.

My experience as an Advocacy Specialist further developed my client-centered approach. I managed a caseload of more than 40 families, assessed individual needs, identified barriers, coordinated services, and maintained detailed case notes and follow-up communication. Working directly with families reinforced the importance of empathy, responsiveness, confidentiality, and creating a structured environment where individuals feel supported.

I am particularly drawn to AWA's mission of supporting adolescents and families during critical moments. My background in public health, family advocacy, healthcare support, and team leadership has taught me that strong operations are essential to delivering quality care. I understand the importance of accurate documentation, timely communication, safety, and coordinated teamwork in protecting both clients and staff.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my program management, supervisory experience, documentation skills, and calm, solutions-oriented approach to AWA. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience can support your team and help ensure the smooth, safe, and effective operation of your programs.

Sincerely,

Helsa Guillaume Clarke

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in a professional position where I can utilize my extensive background in education, behavioral health, case management, supervision, and social services. With 15 years of teaching experience, including 7 years in supervisory and leadership capacities, combined with 7 years as a Regional Case Manager serving juveniles across six South Florida counties, I bring a comprehensive understanding of educational, behavioral, mental health, medical, and social-service systems. My experience has equipped me with the ability to lead teams, manage complex cases, build collaborative relationships, conduct detailed assessments, maintain regulatory compliance, and advocate effectively for individuals and families.

Throughout my career in education, I have developed strong skills in instruction, assessment, intervention planning, documentation, staff collaboration, and program oversight. My seven years in supervisory roles strengthened my leadership abilities and provided extensive experience supporting staff, monitoring performance, resolving challenges, implementing policies and procedures, and ensuring that organizational expectations and professional standards were consistently met.

A significant component of my professional experience has been my seven years as a Regional Case Manager responsible for juveniles determined to be mentally incompetent to proceed, with responsibilities spanning six counties throughout South Florida. In this role, I worked closely with juvenile clients, families, behavioral health professionals, attorneys, court personnel, service providers, and other stakeholders. I established and fostered professional relationships with the judicial systems in each county, requiring effective communication, sound judgment, confidentiality, cultural competency, and the ability to navigate complex systems while maintaining the best interests of the youth at the center of my work.

My case management background extends beyond juvenile services and includes mental health and medical case management across various age groups and populations. I have experience coordinating services, identifying client needs, connecting individuals with appropriate resources, monitoring treatment and service plans, advocating for clients, documenting progress, and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to assess situations holistically and develop practical, individualized approaches to addressing behavioral health, medical, educational, family, and social-service needs.

I also bring extensive experience conducting and interpreting assessments, maintaining comprehensive case records, monitoring documentation, and preparing for annual audits of client files. I understand the importance of accurate, timely, and compliant documentation and have consistently worked to ensure that records meet organizational, contractual, and regulatory expectations. My experience includes reviewing files for completeness and accuracy, identifying deficiencies, following corrective processes, maintaining confidentiality, and ensuring that required services and documentation are properly tracked.

Academically, I hold a Master of Science in Reading Education and a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology, providing me with a strong foundation in educational development, human behavior, assessment, learning, and intervention. I am also currently pursuing a Master of Social Work (MSW), which I expect to obtain in December 2026. This combination of education, psychology, social work, case management, and leadership experience has given me a multidisciplinary perspective that allows me to understand individuals not simply from one professional lens, but within the broader context of their educational, behavioral, medical, family, and social environments.

I am particularly proud of my ability to build meaningful professional partnerships while simultaneously maintaining accountability and high standards. Whether working with judicial professionals, educators, clinicians, families, community providers, or organizational leadership, I approach each relationship with professionalism, respect, and a solutions-oriented mindset. I am comfortable managing competing priorities, working with complex and high-needs populations, meeting deadlines, maintaining detailed records, and adapting to changing organizational and client needs.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my 15 years of educational experience, 7 years of supervisory leadership, 7 years of regional case management, behavioral health and medical case management expertise, assessment and audit experience, and multidisciplinary academic preparation to your organization. I am confident that my combination of leadership, case management, advocacy, assessment, compliance, and relationship-building skills would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team and the individuals you serve.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, qualifications, and commitment to service can support the goals of your organization. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely, 


Sandra Cowell, MS CBHCM

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Facility Manager role with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With more than 10 years of experience managing operations in fast-paced, highly regulated environments, I have developed a strong ability to lead teams, coordinate complex daily workflows, manage competing priorities, and maintain structure and accountability in environments where accuracy, communication, and responsiveness are essential.

In my current leadership role, I serve as a central point of coordination for daily team operations. I oversee staffing needs, scheduling, onboarding, training, performance management, workflow monitoring, and operational follow-up. I regularly identify gaps or issues that could impact productivity or service delivery, determine the appropriate course of action, and work with team members and leadership to resolve them quickly and effectively.

A significant part of my experience involves working in compliance-driven environments where accurate documentation, timely follow-up, and attention to detail are critical. I monitor performance and quality metrics, review documentation for accuracy, maintain standard operating procedures, and ensure team members understand and follow established processes. I am comfortable identifying potential compliance concerns, escalating issues appropriately, and taking corrective action before they become larger operational problems.

I also understand the importance of effective communication when managing a team in a fast-paced environment. I regularly lead team meetings and huddles, provide coaching and feedback, delegate responsibilities, and hold team members accountable for expectations and deadlines. When unexpected issues arise, I remain calm, assess the situation, prioritize what needs immediate attention, and communicate clear direction to keep operations moving forward.

Many of the skills I have developed translate directly to AWA's program environment. I have experience coordinating people and resources, managing daily workflows, maintaining accurate records, supporting compliance requirements, resolving operational barriers, and ensuring that teams have the structure and direction they need to provide consistent service.

What particularly interests me about AWA is the opportunity to apply my operational leadership experience in an organization focused on supporting adolescents and their families. I understand that strong operations are essential to creating a safe, organized, and dependable environment for both clients and staff. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, accountability, organization, and hands-on leadership style to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and operational leadership experience I can contribute to AWA's continued success.

Sincerely,

Crystal Dave

This experience has been incredibly valuable and has allowed me to grow both professionally and personally while developing a deeper understanding of the needs of the individuals and families I serve.
When I began this position, I anticipated maintaining a caseload of approximately 30 clients, which I understood would allow me to provide each individual with the attention, advocacy, and support they deserve. However, my caseload has grown to approximately 50 clients. While I remain committed to serving my clients effectively, the increased workload has made it challenging to provide the level of individualized service I believe is essential to being an effective case manager.
I initially intended to supplement my income by working a second job, but the demands of my current caseload make that unrealistic. My current salary is approximately $45,000 annually, and I am seeking an opportunity that provides greater financial stability while allowing me to remain fully committed to a career in human services.
I am passionate about helping others and want to continue building my career in this field. I am looking for an organization where I can bring my experience, compassion, and dedication to the work while earning a salary that provides the financial stability necessary for me to focus fully on my professional responsibilities. My goal is to find a position where I can be fully engaged, give 100% to the individuals I serve, and continue growing as a human services professional.

In my previous position, I served as a Residential Program Director with Sunrise Community, where I was responsible for overseeing two group homes and supervising a team of approximately 20 staff members. My salary was $45,000 yearly but was raised to $55,000 after 3 months. This role was highly rewarding and provided me with valuable experience supporting individuals with mental health and intellectual disabilities. I found the work especially meaningful because it allowed me to advocate for the individuals we served while ensuring they received appropriate care, support, and services.

During my tenure (July 2024-2025), one of the homes under my supervision was closed, and I was subsequently transferred to Miami to manage two additional residential homes. This transition presented several significant operational challenges, including the need to work directly on the staff floor while simultaneously fulfilling my managerial responsibilities. In addition, there were ongoing operational and compliance concerns within the homes that created potential liabilities.

I made every effort to address these concerns through the appropriate management channels and advocated for the necessary corrective actions. Unfortunately, when several of the issues remained unresolved despite my efforts to bring them to upper management's attention, I ultimately made the difficult decision to leave the organization.

Despite the circumstances surrounding my departure, I remain grateful for the experience and the opportunity to serve individuals with disabilities. The position strengthened my leadership, problem-solving, staff-management, advocacy, and crisis-management skills, all of which continue to shape my approach to working in human services.

Sincerely,
Nana Mensah Jr., MHA

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Facility Manager – Adolescent Mental Health position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I bring a multidisciplinary background in healthcare operations, integrative health and wellness, behavioral health support, program development, client and family engagement, and healthcare coordination. Throughout my career, I have focused on creating organized, compassionate, patient-centered environments while building strong relationships with healthcare professionals, staff, clients, and families.

In my current role as Lead Integrative Therapist with CareRite Centers in South Florida, I deliver and coordinate integrative health and wellness programming across multiple skilled nursing and rehabilitation facilities. I work closely with facility administrators, nursing leadership, interdisciplinary clinical teams, staff, residents, caregivers, and families to support consistent program delivery, staff engagement, health education, and patient-centered care. Working across multiple facilities has strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, adapt quickly to different operational environments, identify needs, communicate effectively with leadership, and maintain continuity and quality across programs.

A significant part of my work involves supporting individuals and families navigating cognitive, emotional, behavioral, and psychosocial challenges. I also provide staff-focused wellness and educational initiatives designed to strengthen engagement, stress management, communication, and the overall care environment. My approach combines compassion with structure, accountability, clear communication, and a strong focus on the individual experience.

My previous healthcare experience also includes client services and healthcare support coordination involving multiple behavioral health and substance-use treatment facilities. In that environment, I gained valuable exposure to behavioral healthcare operations, insurance and benefits processes, documentation, provider and facility communication, multidisciplinary coordination, and the importance of maintaining organized services for individuals and families experiencing complex circumstances.

Education and continuous professional development are also central to my career. I am currently completing my Bachelor of Health Services Administration at Florida International University. My additional healthcare education includes training through Harvard Medical School, Mayo Clinic, the National Institutes of Health and National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and The University of Texas at Austin School of Nursing. My studies have included behavioral and integrative health, healthcare leadership, quality improvement, dementia and person-centered care, gerontology, infection prevention, clinical care for autistic adults, palliative care, and healthcare program improvement.

What particularly attracts me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to bring together the areas that have defined my professional development: behavioral health, healthcare operations, program leadership, staff engagement, multidisciplinary collaboration, and compassionate care. I understand that effective behavioral healthcare requires more than efficient operations. It requires an environment where clients and families feel respected, staff feel supported, communication remains strong, and every part of the organization works toward a consistent standard of care.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare experience, leadership abilities, organizational skills, bilingual English-Spanish communication, and commitment to quality and compassionate care to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am prepared for the next step in my career and would be honored to contribute to an organization dedicated to supporting adolescents and their families during such an important period of their lives.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience can contribute to the continued success of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Piero Ballen

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Facility Manager – Adolescent Mental Health position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With more than 30 years of experience in youth development, recreation, program administration, community services, and nonprofit leadership, I bring a strong combination of operational leadership, staff supervision, program management, and a genuine commitment to supporting young people and their families.

Throughout my career, I have worked in environments where safety, structure, accountability, and positive relationships are essential. As Director of Programs with Empowering Youth Inc., I have managed programs serving children, adolescents, and families, including mental health and CIFFTA programming in Miami-Dade County. My responsibilities have included program operations, staffing, compliance, reporting, budgets, contracts, community partnerships, and coordination with schools and government agencies.

My previous experience with OIC of South Florida and the City of Oakland Park further developed my ability to manage facilities, supervise employees, coordinate programs, address operational challenges, and maintain professional relationships with families, community partners, and other stakeholders. I understand that a facility serving adolescents in a mental health environment requires a leader who can balance compassion with structure and who understands the importance of safety, confidentiality, professionalism, and consistency.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because I believe adolescents need environments where they feel safe, respected, heard, and supported. A well-managed facility can have a significant impact on the quality of care and the experience of both clients and staff. I would bring a hands-on leadership approach, strong organizational skills, and the ability to identify problems, develop solutions, and ensure that daily operations support the organization's clinical and programmatic mission.

I also bring extensive experience working with multidisciplinary partners, managing competing priorities, preparing reports, monitoring budgets and contracts, supervising staff, and maintaining compliance with organizational and governmental requirements. I am comfortable working in fast-paced environments and understand the importance of remaining calm, professional, and solution-oriented when challenges arise.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience in youth development, mental health programming, facility operations, staff leadership, and community engagement to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am confident that my background and commitment to serving young people would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your organization.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and leadership can support Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families you serve.

Sincerely,
John Jones

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. My background in healthcare talent acquisition, public health, and relationship management has provided me with extensive experience working within healthcare environments, communicating with diverse populations, and building meaningful professional relationships.

Throughout my recruiting career, I have supported healthcare organizations by sourcing and engaging physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, allied health professionals, and other healthcare talent. I have developed experience using applicant tracking systems, LinkedIn Recruiter, PracticeMatch, PracticeLink, DocCafe, Boolean sourcing, candidate outreach, and other recruiting technologies to identify and connect with qualified professionals. My work has required strong organization, responsiveness, discretion, follow-through, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

I am particularly interested in Adolescent Wellness Academy because of its emphasis on creating a safe, supportive, and judgment-free environment for adolescents and their families. AWA takes a family-centered approach and provides structured programs designed to help teens develop coping skills, resilience, and a sense of connection.

My Bachelor of Science in Public Health and Nursing has also given me a broader understanding of the factors that influence health and well-being, including the importance of communication, access to care, community support, and prevention. Combined with my healthcare recruiting experience, this perspective has helped me understand the importance of connecting people with the right resources and professionals.

I would be excited to contribute my healthcare industry knowledge, relationship-building skills, professionalism, and ability to work effectively with diverse teams to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Dear Hiring Manager,
As a compassionate and detail-oriented mental health professional with over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, I was excited to see the admissions coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a proven track record in admissions coordination, client assessments, case management, and supporting individuals and families through recovery, I am eager to bring my empathy, clinical insight, and organizational strengths to your team.
From 2014 to 2024, I held progressive roles in residential treatment and case management, including serving as Admissions Specialist at Monte Nido, where I managed the full admission process — from initial inquiries and biopsychosocial assessments to insurance coordination and client transitions. I later provided direct care as a Case Manager and Group Facilitator at Recovery is a Beach and Rise Malibu, conducting assessments (including PHQ-9 and GAD-7), developing individualized care plans, facilitating groups, and ensuring seamless coordination with multidisciplinary teams. After welcoming my son in late 2024, I chose to take dedicated time off of work to care for my family. I am now fully refreshed and excited to return to the field with even greater enthusiasm and commitment.
My personal recovery of 22 years continues to fuel my dedication to meeting clients and families with genuine understanding and hope. Whether building rapport with clients and their loved ones, highlighting and explaining the benefits of a particular treatment program, actively listening, collaborating with clinical teams, or maintaining thorough documentation, I bring both professional expertise and heartfelt empathy to every interaction. I am confident my combination of direct admissions experience, case management, group facilitation, strong communication skills, and recovery-informed perspective would enable me to contribute meaningfully from day one.
Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you soon.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Adolescent Services Manager position at AWA. With several years of experience leading youth programs, supervising staff, coordinating daily operations, and creating structured and supportive environments for adolescents, I believe my background in education and youth program management would translate well to this role.

In my current role as an Assistant Director with New York Edge, I help oversee the daily operations of a large after-school program serving more than 500 middle school students. I supervise and coach staff, coordinate schedules and staffing coverage, support program implementation, and step into a site leadership role when the Program Director is unavailable. This experience has strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain structure, address challenges in real time, and ensure that both staff and students have the support they need to be successful.

A significant part of my role involves working directly with adolescents and creating an environment where students feel supported while clear expectations and boundaries are maintained. I have experience responding to behavioral concerns, communicating with families and staff, addressing incidents appropriately, and following established policies and safety procedures. I understand the importance of remaining calm and solutions-focused when unexpected situations arise, while also ensuring consistency and accountability across a team.

I also bring strong organizational and administrative skills. From managing staff schedules and daily program logistics to monitoring attendance, coordinating activities, communicating with multiple stakeholders, and ensuring that program expectations are followed, I am accustomed to keeping complex youth programs running smoothly. I take pride in anticipating potential challenges, identifying solutions, and creating systems that allow both staff and students to have a positive and consistent experience.

My educational background further supports my interest in this position. I hold a Bachelor's degree in Psychology and a Master's degree in School Counseling, which have given me a strong foundation in adolescent development, social-emotional needs, communication, and creating supportive environments for young people. While my professional background has been primarily in education and youth programming rather than clinical mental health services, I am particularly drawn to AWA's focus on providing adolescents and families with a structured, compassionate environment in which they can grow.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my leadership experience, organizational skills, and passion for supporting adolescents to AWA. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to your team and the adolescents and families you serve.

Sincerely,

Leyla Eskinova

position.name: Business Development & Outreach Representative – Substance Use Treatment
position.description:
Outreach Representative – Substance Use Treatment

Palm Beach & North Broward Territory | Full-Time | Field-Based + On-Site | Competitive Base | Commission Eligible

About the Role

Principles Recovery Center is seeking an experienced Outreach Representative to grow trusted referral partnerships throughout Palm Beach County and northern Broward. You will connect hospitals, detox programs, treatment providers, therapists, and community partners with PRC’s adult substance use and co-occurring mental health services.

This role is ideal for someone who already understands the local treatment community, has an established professional network, and believes relationships can create meaningful pathways into recovery.

Backgrounds that translate well: Substance Use Treatment Outreach · Behavioral Health Business Development · Admissions · Referral Relations · Hospital Liaison

What You’ll Do

  • Build and strengthen referral relationships across Palm Beach County and northern Broward
  • Visit hospitals, detox facilities, treatment programs, therapists, and community organizations
  • Educate partners on PRC’s adult PHP and IOP programming and admissions process
  • Identify appropriate referral opportunities and support smooth connections into care
  • Collaborate closely with Admissions to ensure responsive communication and follow-through
  • Represent PRC at provider meetings, professional events, health fairs, and networking opportunities
  • Maintain accurate, same-day CRM documentation of outreach activity and referral progress
  • Develop monthly territory plans and contribute to quarterly growth strategies
  • Monitor referral trends, community needs, and changes within the local treatment landscape

What We’re Looking For

Required

  • 2+ years of business development or outreach experience with a substance use treatment provider
  • Familiarity with the Palm Beach and northern Broward treatment community
  • Active professional relationships with behavioral health providers and referral partners
  • Ability to build trust and communicate credibly with clinical and community partners
  • Strong follow-through, organization, and time management in an autonomous field-based role
  • Residence within or near the assigned territory
  • Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, and ability to pass a Level 2 background screening

Preferred

  • Substance use treatment admissions or referral coordination experience
  • CRM experience using Salesforce, HubSpot, or a similar platform
  • Bilingual English/Spanish proficiency

Principles Recovery Center provides adult PHP and IOP treatment for individuals navigating substance use and co-occurring mental health conditions. Our work is grounded in meaningful relationships, responsive support, and the belief that every connection can open the door to lasting recovery.

Learn More: Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to express my strong interest in joining Principles Recovery Center as a Business Development Representative. I bring nearly a decade immersed in the addiction treatment field, combining hands-on clinical experience with a proven track record of building referral networks and strategic partnerships that drive sustainable growth — including 3+ years of direct outreach experience within behavioral health treatment programs and an established professional referral network across South Florida.
As a Nationally Certified Intervention Professional (NCIP) through The Addictions Academy, I have extensive experience guiding families through the intervention process with compassion, structure, and professional expertise. My approach is grounded in evidence-based practices and a deep understanding of the emotional complexity that surrounds addiction — allowing me to connect with clients and families at their most vulnerable moments and move them toward lasting change.
My clinical foundation is rooted in a Master of Social Work from Tulane University and further reinforced by my Addictions Psychology certification from Stanford University School of Medicine. I am also a Nationally Certified Recovery Coach (NCRC), a Certified Case Manager (CCMC), and a Certified Recovery Peer Advocate — credentials that reflect both my commitment to the field and my ability to deliver care at multiple levels of the recovery continuum.
Throughout my career, I have built and managed referral networks, developed marketing and outreach materials, and cultivated lasting partnerships with hospitals, detox programs, therapists, educational institutions, and community organizations: the same partner base Principles Recovery Center relies on to grow admissions. These relationships have translated directly into census growth and stronger continuum-of-care partnerships; the kind of measurable outcomes that matter most in business development.
Equally important, my clinical background as a Primary Therapist and Recovery Coach gives me firsthand insight into what referral sources, families, and treatment teams need to trust a program. I speak the clinical language fluently, having led group and individual therapy, conducted comprehensive client assessments, and managed complex cases using CBT, MI, and DBT methodologies and credibility that lets me build authentic, lasting relationships other business development professionals can't easily replicate.
Now settled in Miami's Edgewater community, I travel comfortably and consistently throughout the Fort Lauderdale–Miami–Boca Raton corridor and am eager to bring my background in clinical care, partnership development, and outreach strategy to Principles Recovery Center as you continue to expand your reach and impact across South Florida. position.description:
Behavioral Health Recruiter

Fully On-Site | Full-Time | Flexible Monday–Friday Schedule | $25.00/hour | Davie, Florida

About the Role

Lead full-cycle recruiting and shape the new-hire experience through the first 100 days across Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. You’ll use recruiting data, structured interviews, and Topgrading principles to identify people who will strengthen our clinical, operational, administrative, and leadership teams.

We’re looking for a growth-minded recruiter who wants to expand across talent acquisition, employer branding, and employee experience. Every hire matters here; each person welcomed into our village shapes our culture, our teams, and the care our clients receive.

Relevant Backgrounds: Behavioral Health Recruiting · Healthcare Recruiting · Clinical Recruiting · Talent Acquisition · Healthcare Staffing

What You’ll Do

  • Manage full-cycle recruiting from sourcing through offer, clearance, and onboarding
  • Recruit therapists, counselors, case managers, behavioral health technicians, administrative professionals, and leaders
  • Screen and interview candidates using Breezy HR, scorecards, and Topgrading methods
  • Lead hiring huddles and provide managers with candidate recommendations, interview feedback, and recruiting data
  • Coordinate references, background screening, drug testing, credential verification, and onboarding records
  • Track pre-start readiness, training, manager check-ins, new-hire feedback, and 100-day retention
  • Build talent pipelines through job boards, referrals, social media, employer branding, networking, schools, and community events

What We’re Looking For

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience
  • 2+ years of full-cycle recruiting, talent acquisition, or healthcare staffing experience
  • Strong sourcing, interviewing, networking, and relationship-building skills
  • Experience managing multiple openings, deadlines, and hiring metrics
  • Organized, responsive, data-minded, and interested in growing within recruiting and employee experience
  • Ability to work onsite, travel locally, and satisfy DCF and AHCA Level 2 background-screening requirements

Preferred

  • Behavioral health, mental health, substance use treatment, healthcare, or clinical recruiting experience
  • Experience with Breezy HR or another applicant tracking system (ATS)
  • Experience with Topgrading, structured interviewing, onboarding, or credentialing
  • Employer branding, recruitment marketing, social media, or career-fair experience
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish

Schedule and Local Travel

Set your Monday–Friday hours around interviews, recruiting priorities, and events. This is a fully on-site role with some local travel to company locations, schools, career fairs, and community events. Approved business mileage is reimbursed according to company policy.

Who We Are

AWA and PRC provide Partial Hospitalization and Intensive Outpatient care for adolescents and adults navigating mental health, substance use, and co-occurring conditions. We meet clients and families during some of their most critical moments with compassion, structure, and hope. Every person we welcome to our team strengthens our ability to change lives—and this role helps us find them.

Learn More: Adolescent Wellness Academy · Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am excited to apply for a Talent Acquisition, Recruiting, or HR opportunity with your organization. With
experience in recruiting and onboarding within a fast-growing technology startup, client relationship
management at American Express, and multi-unit leadership with H&R; Block, I bring a combination of
recruiting expertise, operational discipline, and a genuine passion for helping people succeed.
In my most recent role as a Recruiting & Onboarding Coordinator at Sunbird, I supported high-volume
recruitment across technical and operational positions while coordinating interviews, managing
candidates through an ATS, supporting requisitions, and helping develop onboarding processes. I
contributed to 100% headcount fulfillment while helping improve employee integration and engagement
metrics by 20%. These experiences strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities,
communicate effectively with candidates and hiring managers, and maintain accuracy in a fast-paced
environment.
My background also includes working directly with clients and leading teams. At American Express, I
managed a high volume of client relationships while consistently exceeding performance expectations,
achieving 105% of targets related to service quality and engagement. At H&R Block, I managed staffing
and recruiting operations across three locations, coordinating interviews and hiring events for more than
50 seasonal employees while supporting training, scheduling, and team development.
What I bring is more than recruiting experience. I bring an ability to build relationships, recognize talent,
solve problems, and create organized processes that help teams perform at their best. I am adaptable,
highly comfortable with technology and modern recruiting tools, and motivated by opportunities where I
can contribute to both people and organizational growth.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring my recruiting, onboarding, leadership, and
relationship-management experience to your team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look
forward to the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your organization.
Sincerely,
Brian Koehn

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am excited to submit my application for opportunities in Human Resources, People Operations, Talent Acquisition, and Employee Relations within your organization. With five years of progressive Human Resources experience across healthcare, staffing, manufacturing, and recruiting, I have built and supported HR functions focused on talent acquisition, employee relations, onboarding, compliance, and operational excellence.
Most recently, I served as a Human Resources Manager, where I established the Human Resources function from the ground up for a growing healthcare staffing organization. I led full-cycle recruitment, implemented HR processes and an Applicant Tracking System (ATS), strengthened compliance practices, and partnered with executive leadership to support workforce planning and organizational growth.
Throughout my career, I have recruited and successfully onboarded more than 100 employees while supporting remote, hybrid, and on-site workforces. My experience includes collaborating with hiring managers, improving recruitment processes, supporting employee relations, maintaining HR compliance, and creating positive employee experiences through structured onboarding and effective communication.
I hold a Master of Business Administration (MBA) with a specialization in Human Resource Management and a Bachelor's degree in Industrial-Organizational Psychology. These academic credentials, combined with my practical HR experience, have prepared me to contribute effectively to high-performing Human Resources teams.
I am excited about the opportunity to bring my HR experience, collaborative approach, and commitment to continuous improvement to an organization that values its people and invests in building a strong workplace culture.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience can contribute to your Human Resources team. I look forward to speaking with you.
Sincerely,
Christopher Alvarado

September 1, 2026 

 Adolescent Wellness Academy 
 Davie, FL 

 Dear Hiring Team, 
 I am excited to apply for the Behavioral Health Recruiter position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am a full-cycle recruiter and recent psychology graduate from Florida Atlantic University, and this opportunity immediately stood out to me because it brings together my professional recruiting experience with my academic background in psychology and human behavior. 
In my current role as a Full-Cycle Recruiter with NuLogic Business Solutions, I support recruiting across multiple client accounts from candidate sourcing and screening through interview coordination, documentation, onboarding, and follow-up. I manage high-volume candidate communication, evaluate qualifications against role requirements, maintain organized recruiting records in HubSpot, and coordinate onboarding using tools including DocuSign, Zoom, Microsoft Office, and Google Workspace. I also have prior full-cycle recruiting experience with The Insurance Pipeline, where I supported high-volume hiring for positions ranging from entry-level through management. 
My psychology degree adds a perspective that I believe is especially relevant in a behavioral health environment. Through my coursework and research experience at Florida Atlantic University, I developed a strong understanding of human behavior, research methods, structured procedures, data interpretation, confidentiality, and professional communication with participants. While my recruiting background has not been specifically within behavioral health, I am genuinely interested in applying my recruiting skills in a field that connects closely with my education. 
I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my recruiting, candidate relationship, onboarding, and organizational experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center while continuing to grow within talent acquisition and employee experience. Thank you for your consideration. I would be glad to discuss how my background could support your hiring goals and the teams serving your clients. 

Sincerely, 
Tiffanie Bailey

position.name: Behavioral Health Technician
position.description:
Behavioral Health Technician

On-Site | Full-Time | Schedule Tuesday to Saturday 7:00am - 3:30pm | Compensation: This role starts at $17.00/hour during the onboarding and training period. After successful completion of training and certification in core responsibilities, pay increases to $19.00/hour.

About the Role

You are a frontline member of the PRC care team. You support adult clients through structured recovery programming — maintaining safety, accountability, and a therapeutic environment from the moment your shift starts. This role requires calm under pressure, strong documentation habits, and genuine commitment to the people you serve.

Backgrounds that translate well: Behavioral Health Tech · Direct Care · Substance Use Treatment · Residential Support · Crisis Stabilization

What You'll Do

  • Supervise and support adult clients throughout daily programming
  • Conduct regular headcounts, rounds, and safety checks
  • Collect and document urine drug screens in accordance with policy
  • Complete shift notes, room checks, incident reports, and behavior documentation accurately and on time
  • Maintain cleanliness and order of all shared program spaces
  • Enforce program rules with professionalism and respect — firm, never punitive
  • Collaborate with therapists, medical staff, and leadership across shifts
  • Participate in team meetings and shift-change debriefs
  • Escort clients to appointments or activities as needed

What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years of experience as a BHT or in a similar direct care role
  • Experience working with adult clients in a substance use treatment setting
  • Strong documentation habits — shift notes, incident reports, and UA logs completed accurately and on time
  • Calm, boundaries, and professional under pressure
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • CPR/First Aid certified or able to obtain upon hire
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Eligible for Level II background screening and drug test
  • Available full-time for Tuesday–Saturday schedule

PRC is an adult behavioral health organization operating PHP and IOP programs across South Florida. We exist to serve clients and families at their most critical moments — and this role supports that mission on the ground every day.

Learn More: Principles Recovery Center

position.name: Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health
position.description:
Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health

On Site | North Carolina | Full-Time W-2 Beginning January 2027 | Competitive Compensation | Pre-Launch Fractional or Contract Opportunity

About the Role

Adolescent Wellness Academy is expanding into North Carolina. We are looking for an experienced Clinic Director to lead the launch and ongoing success of our first facility in the state.

You will oversee the clinic’s performance across four pillars: clinical excellence, client experience, employee experience, and business health. This role is ideal for a strong clinical leader who can build an exceptional team, create a values-driven culture, and deliver meaningful results for adolescents and families.

Backgrounds that translate well: Adolescent Mental Health Leadership · PHP/IOP · Behavioral Health Operations · Clinical Program Development · Residential Treatment

What You’ll Lead

  • Launch and ongoing performance of AWA’s first North Carolina facility
  • Clinical quality, client outcomes, team experience, and financial health
  • Recruitment, development, and performance management of the clinical and operational teams
  • Admissions, treatment planning, clinical progress, crisis response, and discharge coordination
  • Documentation quality, regulatory compliance, accreditation readiness, and risk management
  • Strong partnerships with families, providers, and community referral sources
  • Continuous improvement of programming, systems, and clinic performance

How We Lead

We believe great leadership is people-first, clear, and accountable. Our leaders practice radical candor, provide consistent feedback, address performance directly, and create an environment where people feel supported and challenged to grow.

Our values guide how we work: Dare to Grow. Contribute to the Whole. Choose Kindness. Spread Optimism. Deliver Results.

What We’re Looking For

  • Independently licensed behavioral health professional in North Carolina, such as an LCMHC, LCSW, LMFT, or equivalent
  • Master’s degree in a related clinical field
  • 5+ years of behavioral health experience
  • 2+ years of clinical or operational leadership experience
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing performance
  • Strong knowledge of clinical quality, compliance, and behavioral health operations
  • Adolescent PHP/IOP experience strongly preferred
  • Program launch or expansion experience preferred
  • Qualified Supervisor status preferred
  • Ability to travel occasionally to Florida for company-sponsored training

The full-time W-2 position is expected to begin in January 2027. Fractional or contract work may be available beforehand to support launch planning, program development, recruitment, and training.

AWA provides specialized PHP and IOP mental health services for adolescents and families. We are building thoughtful, high-performing programs where exceptional care and exceptional workplace culture go hand in hand.

Learn More: Adolescent Wellness Academy
